scope.question: Do employee-elected works councils possess enforceable, pre-action authority over the introduction and use of technical monitoring systems, and did that authority produce an observed binding change in one exact deployment?

sources.title: Works Constitution Act § 7 — voting eligibility
supports: employees aged sixteen or older in the establishment are eligible to vote in works-council elections
certain agency workers become eligible after more than three months in the establishment
does_not_support: universal works-council coverage in every establishment
individual employee veto over a technical system
the composition of a particular council

sources.title: Works Constitution Act § 14 — election rules
supports: works councils are elected directly by secret ballot
employees with voting rights and represented unions may submit candidate lists
statutory procedures govern representative selection
does_not_support: equal participation in practice
absence of turnout, representation or capture problems
direct election of every central or combine works-council member

sources.title: Works Constitution Act § 87 — binding co-determination
supports: the works council has a co-determination right over introduction and use of technical devices designed to monitor employee behavior or performance
when employer and council do not agree, a conciliation committee decides
the conciliation award replaces agreement between employer and council
does_not_support: co-determination over every corporate objective or product feature
individual consent by every affected employee
data ownership, source-code access, compensation or value recovery

sources.title: Works Constitution Act § 23 — enforcement and representative accountability
supports: employees, employers or represented unions may seek removal or dissolution for gross council-duty violations
works councils or represented unions may seek court orders against gross employer violations
court orders may be backed by fines
does_not_support: easy or equal access to enforcement
automatic relief for every co-determination violation
complete accountability of central or combine councils to every local worker

sources.title: BAG 1 ABR 7/15 — Facebook visitor-post monitoring function
supports: a combine works council challenged an employer-operated Facebook visitor-post function that exposed employee behavior and performance
the court classified the function as a technical monitoring facility under § 87(1)(6)
the employer was ordered to disable the function unless the council consented or the conciliation committee supplied a substitute decision
the order changed a specific system function prospectively
does_not_support: a requirement to delete the entire Facebook page
individual employee control over each post
co-governance over Facebook as a platform
data deletion, compensation or value recovery

sources.title: BAG 1 ABR 20/21 — Microsoft Office 365 central-tenant co-determination
supports: Office 365 introduction and use were subject to § 87(1)(6) co-determination
centralized monitoring capability made the matter company-wide
the central works council rather than the local works council held competence
does_not_support: the terms of the final Office 365 agreement
a local-worker veto over the central tenant
source-code, data-ownership or deletion rights
proof that the system was rejected or materially reconfigured

sources.title: BAG 1 ABR 31/19 — email-system co-determination and deletion limit
supports: email software capable of generating performance or behavior information is subject to co-determination
a works council may seek cessation of a technical monitoring system introduced or used without co-determination
the council had already exercised its co-determination right for the email applications in that case
does_not_support: a general right to compel third-party deletion of worker data
an individual employee veto
co-governance over all later uses of the data without a new legal or factual basis

sources.title: BAG 1 ABR 16/23 — headset monitoring without recording
supports: a headset system enabling supervisors to listen to employee communications is a monitoring system subject to co-determination even when conversations are not recorded
the right is aimed at protecting employees from becoming objects of opaque technical monitoring
does_not_support: success of every requested injunction
worker control over the employer's entire communications architecture
data rights where no data are retained
